audits.title: ThTP6.10 A multi-specialty clinical audit to assess true surgical site infection incidence at a district general hospital in Kent
audits.standard: National targets: SSI rate < 1% after clean and < 10% after clean-contaminated surgery
audits.setting: Multi-specialty surgery, district general hospital, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Overall SSI rate 14.5% (n = 138); general surgery 18.1% (45/249), elective 12.84% and emergency 22.14%; paediatric surgery 4.3% (2/47).

audits.intervention: Oxford 8-point SSI reduction bundle implemented; re-audit scheduled for 2023.
audits.other_findings: 38 SSIs were found only by follow-up telephone calls; in orthopaedics procedure type correlated with SSI (Rs 0.961, P < 0.001).
audits.citation: Gardner A, Tamrakar A, Wates E, Atherley I, Nebo V, Fernandes R. ThTP6.10 A multi-specialty clinical audit to assess true surgical site infection incidence at a district general hospital in Kent. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.304.

audits.standard: WHO global guidelines for the prevention of surgical site infection
audits.setting: 45 hospitals in 12 countries via the Reconstructive Surgery Trials Network

audits.title: WTP8.4 Head and Neck Surgical Site Infections: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.setting: Tertiary centre, Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 7 SSIs; 7/14 diabetic patients received prophylactic antibiotics; 2 diabetic patients had early post-operative infection.

audits.intervention: Flow-chart antibiotic prophylaxis protocol and presentation at a local meeting.

cycle2.result: 6 SSIs; 16/19 diabetic patients received prophylactic antibiotics; 0 diabetic infections.

audits.other_findings: SSI was more likely with surgical drains (8/94, p=0.008498) and prophylaxis in this group was inconsistent in both cycles.
audits.citation: Seago I, Dunne H, Bidaye R, Masterson L. WTP8.4 Head and Neck Surgical Site Infections: A Quality Improvement Project. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.233.

audits.title: 1084 Clinical Audit of Surgical Site Infection in Emergency General Surgery Unit at London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust
audits.standard: NICE NG125 surgical site infection guideline (target 100%)
audits.setting: Emergency General Surgery Unit, Northwick Park Hospital, London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Pre-op nose swab 61%, perioperative showering 44%, theatre wear 100%, jewellery removal advice 97%, informed about pre-op antibiotics 66.67%, intra-op antibiotics 14.29%, closure method 77.14%, wound dressing education 49.29%; SSI rate 6.76%.

audits.other_findings: Shortfalls were attributed to communication; a checklist and patient leaflets before discharge were recommended.
audits.citation: Asogwa A, Anyaele N, Ilham A, Mazhar M. 1084 Clinical Audit of Surgical Site Infection in Emergency General Surgery Unit at London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.416.

audits.title: SP5.2 - Reducing Elective Colorectal Surgical Site Infections with Change of Gloves and Instruments Prior to Abdominal Closure; A Multicycle Audit
audits.standard: Change of gloves and instruments before abdominal closure (ChEETAh trial); 30-day SSI rate
audits.setting: Local colorectal unit, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust; elective colorectal surgery
audits.intervention: Change of gloves and instruments by the whole scrub team before abdominal closure, then reinforcement with team education.

cycle2.result: SSI rate 15%, sustained across 6 months after intervention.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles over 11 months; SSI fell to 23% after COGI implementation before the reinforcement cycle.
audits.citation: Walsh K. SP5.2 - Reducing Elective Colorectal Surgical Site Infections with Change of Gloves and Instruments Prior to Abdominal Closure; A Multicycle Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.055.

audits.title: Seeking solutions: scaling-up audit as a quality improvement tool for infection control in Gujarat, India.
audits.standard: CDC guidelines for surgical site infection prevention
audits.setting: General surgical unit, Civil Hospital Ahmedabad, scaled up to district state hospitals
audits.intervention: Surveillance and hospital epidemiology, practice reforms and monthly and annual review meetings.

cycle2.result: 88% decrease in infection rate in the surgical unit; 67% reduction after department-wide roll-out.

audits.other_findings: Later scaled up across the state.
audits.citation: Anchalia MM, D'Ambruoso L. Seeking solutions: scaling-up audit as a quality improvement tool for infection control in Gujarat, India. Int J Qual Health Care. 2011;23(4):464-470. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzr007. PMID: 21486857.

audits.title: Reducing Surgical Site Infections in Neurosurgery During the Intra-operative Phase: An Audit of National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guideline Adherence at a Major Trauma Centre.
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on intra-operative surgical site infection prevention (19 parameters)
audits.setting: Neurosurgery department, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust major trauma centre

cycle1.result: Antibiotic prophylaxis information 44%; bodywash 14%; antiseptic application time 12%; double gloving 36%; antimicrobial sutures 2%.

audits.intervention: Targeted interventions and education (details not given in abstract).

cycle2.result: Antibiotic prophylaxis information 90%; bodywash 80%; antiseptic application time 80%; double gloving 44%; antimicrobial sutures 30%.

audits.other_findings: Double gloving and antimicrobial suture use remained low.

audits.title: Evaluating and Improving Surgical Site Infection Prevention: Outcomes of a Two-Cycle Audit and Targeted Interventions in a Low-Resource Setting.
audits.standard: International SSI prevention guidelines (not named in abstract)
audits.setting: Kasr El Ainy Teaching Hospital, Cairo

cycle1.result: SSI rate 12.6%; prolonged postoperative antibiotic use 85.7%; awareness of intraoperative SAP 72.3%; clippers for hair removal 33.7%; intraoperative hair removal 10%; intraoperative warming 47.7%; aseptic technique awareness among junior doctors 36.3%.

audits.intervention: Educational sessions, posters and hands-on training.

cycle2.result: SSI rate 6.6%; awareness of intraoperative SAP 100%; clippers 72.1%; intraoperative hair removal 91.8%; intraoperative warming 87.7% (all p < 0.05); aseptic technique awareness 81.9%.

audits.other_findings: 225 patients and 229 healthcare providers in total across both cycles; knowledge assessed by questionnaire.
audits.citation: Busada BJ. Evaluating and Improving Surgical Site Infection Prevention: Outcomes of a Two-Cycle Audit and Targeted Interventions in a Low-Resource Setting. Cureus. 2024;16(12):e75962. doi:10.7759/cureus.75962. PMID: 39698193.

audits.title: A Clinical Audit of Surgical Site Infection Surveillance in a Maxillo-Facial and Oral Surgery Unit in an Academic Hospital Complex in South Africa.
audits.standard: NICE guideline NG125 on surgical site infection
audits.setting: Maxillofacial and Oral Surgery unit, academic hospital complex (Steve Biko Hospital, Pretoria)

cycle1.result: Composite compliance with process indicators 39.86% (95% CI 37.25-42.46); surgical site infection incidence 14.81% (n = 8).

audits.other_findings: Head and neck malignancy resection contributed 50% of SSI cases; lapses in aseptic technique and wound management were noted.
audits.citation: Nokaneng EN, Holloway SL. A Clinical Audit of Surgical Site Infection Surveillance in a Maxillo-Facial and Oral Surgery Unit in an Academic Hospital Complex in South Africa. Int Wound J. 2025;22(5):e70196. doi:10.1111/iwj.70196. PMID: 40289454.

audits.title: A closed-loop audit to assess and improve surgical site infection rates across all surgical specialties.
audits.setting: All surgical specialties, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
audits.intervention: Perioperative seven-point SSI reduction checklist in elective surgical theatres

cycle2.result: Elective general surgery SSI rate 1%; checklist completion 47%

audits.other_findings: 38 additional SSIs (22.46% of SSIs) found only by telephone follow-up; the one SSI at re-audit had no completed checklist.

audits.title: Implementation of an Evidence-Based Quality Improvement Protocol to Reduce Surgical Site Infections after Lower Extremity Bypass Surgery.
audits.standard: Skin preparation and clipping standards; SSI prevention bundle
audits.setting: Tertiary academic medical centre, Duke University (VQI registry)

cycle1.result: SSI incidence 23.2% (120/517; 85 superficial, 35 deep); internal audit showed suboptimal compliance with skin preparation and clipping standards.

audits.intervention: SSI bundle: antibiotic order set tailored to local antibiogram, skin preparation and hair removal training, glycaemic control, normothermia and chlorhexidine prescrub.
audits.citation: Kim Y, Cui CL, Seymour KA, Seidelman JL, Johnson AP. Implementation of an Evidence-Based Quality Improvement Protocol to Reduce Surgical Site Infections after Lower Extremity Bypass Surgery. Ann Vasc Surg. 2026;127:274-280. doi:10.1016/j.avsg.2026.02.014. PMID: 41692164.
